# Knowledge Base Workflow: Requirements Discovery

Modular workflow file for a unified web workspace (`prompts/project/`). Apply `INSTRUCTIONS.md` (System Prompt / Custom Instructions) and read `refinement-core.md` ("Socratic examination", "Glossary format", "ADR format", "Requirements rigor", "Anti-patterns", and "Questionnaire") plus any product context in the Knowledge Base (`CONTEXT.md`, `product-overview.md`, ADRs, and reference documents) before executing Step 1 below.

# Workflow: Requirements Discovery

Convert unstructured stakeholder input into traceable requirements through **socratic examination**. You are not a transcriber: capture what was stated and what was implied, flag ambiguities, and produce candidate stories that `/refine-story` carries to sprint planning. What the input does not support does not enter; what it hints at enters as a grounded inference; what it leaves open becomes a question.

Input: what the PO provides in this conversation


## Steps

1. **Load and triage.** Read the input, `CONTEXT.md`, and apply the "Requirements rigor" section of `refinement-core.md`. Scan for anti-patterns (see the "Anti-patterns" section of `refinement-core.md`) and terms that always trigger questions: this scan grounds triage. Classify by counting excerpts, not text volume: USABLE (every excerpt structures a requirement), PARTIALLY USABLE (at least one excerpt structures a requirement and at least one does not), UNUSABLE (no excerpt structures a requirement). UNUSABLE: state this with excerpt-by-excerpt rationale, list 3 to 5 minimal questions with recipients (whoever provided the input, unless a domain role in the glossary is identifiable), write a questionnaire following the "Questionnaire" section of `refinement-core.md`, inform the user that `/requirements-discovery` will re-run with responses, and stop without publishing further artifacts; filler stories help no one. PARTIAL: proceed, and the final artifact opens with a list of unused excerpts and what is missing in each.
   Completed when: classification is stated in a single line, followed by excerpt-by-excerpt rationale when not USABLE.

2. **Breadth-first mapping.** Before generating any story, scan the full input: business domains with confidence ratings (High, Medium, Low; Low marks where discovery requires a follow-up conversation), stakeholders with type (business, technical, end-user) and what each advocates, epics with complexity S, M, L, or XL justified in a single line. An excerpt that structures a requirement becomes an epic and is sized now, naming the open questions that could move the size; partial processing holds the excerpts that structure no requirement at all, not the ones whose numbers are still open, because an empty epics table hides exactly the work the examination is about to size. The converse holds with equal force: an excerpt you marked as structuring no requirement never becomes an epic, however sizable it looks, and the complexity is one letter, with the open questions named beside it rather than a range of letters standing in for the decision. When input is second-hand, the note-taker enters the stakeholders table with type "source". Two voices in opposing positions on the same requirement: add `[CONFLICT]`, recording both positions without resolving unilaterally. A requirement stated by a single voice receives `[VALIDATE WITH TEAM]` where confirmation is critical: unmet role needs, scope decisions made by non-decision-makers; do not mark everything when two voices address disjoint topics. Business needs and technical constraints originate from different stakeholders and carry different weight: distinguish them.
   Completed when: each input excerpt is mapped to a domain and epic, or listed as unexploited.

3. **Search for facts before asking.** Check available context (glossary, `product-overview.md`, ADRs, previous artifacts, and documents provided by the PO or stored in the Knowledge Base): does the mentioned integration already exist? Is the threshold already implemented? A found fact becomes a recommended answer with cited source. Search is restricted to what the PO provided or stored in the Knowledge Base; if nothing is found, state this in a single line at the top of round 1.
   Completed when: each candidate question is marked as answered by a source or open.

4. **Decide scope size.** Apply the "Socratic examination" section of `refinement-core.md` and examine breadth first: the target outcome (what this discovery delivers), scope boundaries, conflicts, and factors affecting epic size. SLAs, channels, and edge cases represent depth and are deferred to step 5. If at the end of this round the frontier fits in a single session, proceed to step 5. If substantial **fog** remains (decisions anticipated but not yet formulateable because they depend on pending answers), open the map: publish the spec following the "Template" section of this workflow file with `Status: open map`, one pending decision per file in `issues/NN-decision-<slug>.md` for each formulateable question, marking `Blocked by:` when dependent on another, and unformulateable fog in "Not yet specified". The distinction between a decision and fog is whether you can formulate the question with precision right now, not whether you can answer it. Mapping the fog is the goal of one session: stop and inform the user that `/requirements-discovery <spec-path>` resolves one decision per session.
   Completed when: either the question frontier fits in a single session, or the spec with an open map and pending decision files exists.

5. **Examine.** Continue rounds of socratic examination in depth, epic by epic: roles, capabilities, outcomes, edge cases suggested by input, dependencies. Domain terms resolved are acknowledged briefly during the round and emitted in the consolidated "Memory / Knowledge Base Updates" section at synthesis. A fact that no attendee knows receives `[TO CONFIRM: whom]` (or `[A CONFIRMAR: quem]`) and leaves the frontier.
   Completed when: the frontier is empty, or the user requests closing.

6. **Synthesize.** Write the discovery spec following the "Template" section of this workflow file and one candidate story per file following the "Candidate story template" section of this workflow file, with `Status: candidate` (or `Status: candidata`) and a preliminary INVEST scorecard. A story failing INVEST does not become a clean card: it remains a candidate with `[INVEST-FAIL]` and resolution guidance. Include undeclared dependencies: integrations, external services, and architectural decisions required for stories to be implementable, each paired with the blocked story and required action. Every line in candidate stories matches input or a valid `[INFERENCE: base]`; unbacked additions are gold plating and must be removed.
   Completed when: spec and candidate stories were delivered in the response, with final disclaimer.

7. **Route open items.** Open `[TO CONFIRM]` items with recipients outside the session: write one questionnaire per recipient following the "Questionnaire" section of `refinement-core.md`, alongside the spec.
   Completed when: no open question remains without a recipient or questionnaire.

8. **Report.** Epics created, candidate story count, open conflicts, and next steps: `/refine-story` per story, or `/requirements-discovery <spec-path>` if map is open.

## Resume decision map

When the argument is a spec with `Status: open map`:

1. Read the full spec and pending decisions in `issues/`. A decision is **unblocked** when it is open and all decisions in `Blocked by:` are resolved.
   Completed when: you know which decisions are unblocked.
2. Select the decision: named by the user, or the first unblocked by number. Mark `Status: in examination` in the file before starting, preventing concurrent sessions from picking it.
   Completed when: file status is updated.
3. Resolve it with socratic examination, one decision per session. Research-type decisions are resolved by reading external sources with citations, without examination rounds. Record the answer directly in the file under `## Answer`, mark `Status: resolved`, and add a line with summary and path in the "Examination decisions" section of the spec.
   Completed when: decision is resolved and linked from spec.
4. The answer may clear surrounding fog: newly formulateable items leave "Not yet specified" and become new pending decisions; items outside the scope move to "Out of scope". Any decision invalidated by the answer is closed with a one-line rationale.
   Completed when: no pending decision contradicts the answer and fog is reassessed.
5. With no pending decisions open: update spec to `Status: in progress` and proceed to step 5 of main steps, in the same session if context permits, otherwise in the next session using the same command.
   Completed when: spec leaves open map status, or you report how many decisions remain.

Pending decision format:

```md
# Decision NN: <question in one sentence>

Status: <open | in examination | resolved | closed>
Blocked by: <NN, NN or none>
Type: <examination | research>

## Question

<what must be decided and why it blocks progress>

## Answer

<upon resolution: decision, who decided, date>
```

## Final notice

Published artifacts only. A triage that stops the workflow and an examination round publish nothing, so they carry no notice: the notice qualifies an artifact someone may circulate.

> ⚠️ This output is an analytical draft. It requires human review before entering a sprint. Validate: technical feasibility, compliance, and unmapped dependencies.

In a pt-BR workspace:

> ⚠️ Este output é um rascunho analítico. Requer revisão humana antes de entrar em sprint. Valide: viabilidade técnica, compliance e dependências não mapeadas.

# Template

# Discovery: <title>

Status: <open map | in progress | completed>
Azure: <epic ID or none>
Source: <input path>, /requirements-discovery session on <YYYY-MM-DD>

## Target Outcome

<what this discovery delivers when finished: one or two lines; all sessions orient around this>

## Partial Processing

<only when triage was PARTIALLY USABLE: input excerpts that generated no artifact and what is missing in each>

## Domains

| Domain | Description | Confidence |
| --- | --- | --- |

## Stakeholders

| Name or role | Type | Advocates for | Conflicts |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

Type: business, technical, end-user, or source (who recorded second-hand input).

## Epics

| Epic | Description | Complexity | Rationale | Domain |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

## Examination Decisions

- <question> -> <answer> (<who>, <date>; pending decision: <path, when originating from map>)

## Pending Decisions

<only with open map: one line per file in issues/NN-decision-<slug>.md, with status>

## Not Yet Specified

<only with open map: scope fog that cannot yet be formulated as a decision; graduated into pending decisions as frontier advances>

## Open Questions

1. [<recipient>] <question> -> <impact if unanswered> (questionnaire: <path or none>)

## Undeclared Dependencies

- <dependency> -> blocks <story> -> <required action>

## Out of Scope

- <item> -> <rationale>

## Primary Flow by Epic

One `flowchart TD` in Mermaid per epic, up to 10 nodes: actors as start and end points, critical steps of happy path, decision nodes only where real branching occurs, `[?]` on nodes with unconfirmed dependencies.

## Candidate Stories

- `issues/01-<slug>.md`: As <role>, I want <capability>. INVEST: <PASS across all | FAIL on <letters>>

> ⚠️ This output is an analytical draft. It requires human review before entering a sprint. Validate: technical feasibility, compliance, and unmapped dependencies.

# Candidate story template

# <ID or short title>: As a <role>, I want <capability>

Status: <READY | REFINE | BLOCKED>
Azure: <work item ID or none>
Source: <path, ID, or "pasted text">, /refine-story session on <YYYY-MM-DD>

## Narrative

As a <role>, I want <capability>, so that <verifiable outcome>.

## INVEST Scorecard

| Criterion | Result | Rationale (when not PASS) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Independent | PASS | |
| Negotiable | | |
| Valuable | | |
| Estimable | | |
| Small | | |
| Testable | | |

## Acceptance Criteria

Scenario: <happy path>
  Given <state>
  When <event>
  Then <verifiable outcome>

Scenario: <edge case>
  Given <state>
  When <event>
  Then <verifiable outcome>

## Original Text Audit

- Narrative: <original> -> <problem> -> <proposed version>
- AC1: BEFORE <text> -> AFTER <scenario> (<violation corrected>)
- Moved: <criterion that was a task, DoD, or orphan> -> <destination>
- Anti-patterns: <type> in <excerpt>

## Examination Decisions

- <question> -> <PO answer> (<who>, <date>)

## Open Questions

1. [<recipient>] <question> -> <impact if unanswered> (questionnaire: <path or none>)

## Notes

- Solutions suggested by PO, preserved as reference: <...>
- Suggested technical tasks, moved from criteria: <...>
- Story points: <team points, if any> [ESTIMATE AT RISK: <gap>] | [CALIBRATE IN PLANNING] <context for team>
- Dependencies: <declared> + <detected [INFERENCE: base]>

## Decomposition Proposal

<only when [DECOMPOSE] or double requirement exists: narrative for each part, mapping of original criteria, which part bears dependencies>

## Verdict

<✅ READY | 🔶 REFINE, unblocks with questions <n>, <m> | ⛔ BLOCKED: <rationale>>

> ⚠️ This output is preparation for refinement, not a replacement. Decisions on scope, value, and priority belong strictly to the PO and team.
